text: A song of ascents. Many a time they have oppressed me from my youth—let Israel now say—

versions.text: A song of ascents. They have often attacked me from my youth—let Israel say it now—
versions.explanation: The verb צרר means to press, harass, or oppress rather than a single act of attack; 'oppressed' better conveys sustained affliction and matches the parallel in verse 2. 'Many a time' also reads with a fuller rhythm for oral delivery.

text: many a time they have oppressed me from my youth, yet they have not prevailed against me.

versions.text: they have often attacked me from my youth, but they have not overcome me.
versions.explanation: For consistency with the corrected wording of verse 1 (the two lines are deliberately identical in Hebrew), and 'prevailed against me' renders לֹא־יָכְלוּ לִי more idiomatically.

text: Plowmen plowed across my back; they cut their furrows long.
But the LORD is righteous; he has cut the ropes of the wicked.
Let all who hate Zion be put to shame and driven back.
Let them be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it is ever pulled up,

versions.text: Let them be like grass on the rooftops, withered before it can grow,
versions.explanation: שָׁלַף means to draw or pull out; the picture is grass that dries up before anyone can even pluck it, which then leads naturally into the harvest imagery of verse 7. 'Before it can grow' loses that connection.

text: which never fills the reaper's hand or the arms of the one who binds the sheaves.
And no one passing by says, "The blessing of the LORD be upon you; we bless you in the name of the LORD."
